_comment: Predicate registry. 'single_valued' predicates auto-retire a prior object during kb_extract consolidation, but only when the subject matches 'single_valued_subjects' — cardinality is a property of (subject, predicate), not of the predicate. A ticket has one status; a repo accumulates them. Everything else keeps both objects. The subject pattern requires a separator or # before the trailing digits, so ticket and issue ids (tkt-4821, pr_#412, svc-api#59) match while names that merely end in a digit (web3, oauth2, sqlite3, es2022) do not. 'preferred' is the vocabulary the extraction prompt asks for, listed here rather than in the prompt so one file owns the predicate names; it is also part of the set an inflected spelling folds onto. 'aliases' fold synonyms onto one canonical predicate so kb_fact_query, which matches on the predicate, does not under-return across synonym silos. Spelling variance that carries no meaning is folded without a list entry: hyphens and apostrophes, and a leading copula ('is_source_of_truth_for' -> 'source_of_truth_for'). Inflection folds too, but only onto a name this file already registers ('deploys_to' -> 'deployed_to'), so an unregistered pair like 'missing'/'missed' is never merged on morphology alone. Nothing single-valued is inflectable, for the same reason no inverse touches one: an inflection of a lifecycle noun is usually a verb meaning something else, and 'tkt-42 states that retries must be bounded' folded onto 'state' would retire the ticket's real lifecycle value to store a quotation. 'inverses' fold the mirrored spelling of a relationship onto one direction, swapping subject and object — the extractor picks a direction per call, and two live rows for one relationship retire independently. Each direction here is the one the graph already uses more, and none of them are single-valued, so the fold cannot change what retires what. 'work_item_object' predicates are asymmetric in roles rather than in spelling: the thing being built goes in the object, so a subject matching 'work_item_pattern' opposite an object that does not is a swapped pair, and folds. Only predicates whose subject must be a BUILDER belong here. A ticket cannot build code, so it cannot be the subject of 'implements' — but it can perfectly well target a problem, so 'addresses', 'fixes', 'closes' and 'resolves' take a work item on either side and are not listed. 'work_item_pattern' is an unanchored token: a subject must equal it, an object need only begin with it, since a work item under a label (tkt-19_step_1) still makes the row a relationship between two work items. It excludes a leading pull-request marker because a PR is an implementer, not a work item, and takes a single word before the separator so a compound id ending in a PR number (tkt-19-repo-pr-277) is not read as one. Extend or override per install with <KB_DIR>/predicates.json using the same shape — 'many_valued' there removes a built-in, 'aliases' and 'inverses' merge with these, 'preferred' and 'work_item_object' add to these lists, and either pattern there replaces the one here.
